sections.heading: Where it comes from
sections.text: The band finished its debut, Are You Experienced, in late April 1967. It kept its regular recording schedule and returned on May 4 to start writing songs for a follow-up LP. The album came out only seven months after the debut's release. The lyrics of Spanish Castle Magic were inspired by a dance hall near Seattle, where Hendrix jammed with other local bands in high school.

sections.heading: Making it
sections.text: Eddie Kramer and George Chkiantz handled the engineering. The basic tracks went onto a four-track recorder, with stereo drums on two tracks, bass on a third and rhythm guitar on a fourth. They mixed that onto a second four-track recorder, leaving two more tracks for lead guitar, vocals and percussion. Hendrix often asked for many re-takes, and Kramer stayed patient with him. Hendrix and Mitchell had begun to voice their own views on creative choices that Chandler had handled on the debut. Chandler had grown tired of the guitarist's perfectionism by October 1967, and Redding began to resent Hendrix's instructions on what he played.

sections.heading: What came after
sections.text: Cat Talking to Me, from that June session, appeared in 2010 on the posthumous album West Coast Seattle Boy: The Jimi Hendrix Anthology. The Hendrix Estate released a box set called The Jimi Hendrix Experience: Bold As Love Sessions on November 7, 2025. The 66 tracks include demos and alternate takes, and the Blu-ray adds a Dolby Atmos mix. Malaysia's Home Ministry banned the album's art after complaints, and some Hindus have since voiced anger over the religious images on the cover.

listen.text: It opens with microphonic and harmonic feedback, and sounds from Hendrix's guitar pan across the stereo field to circle the listener.

On this track Hendrix first uses a Leslie speaker for his guitar, a revolving speaker that gives a wavering effect.

paragraphs: Axis: Bold as Love is the second studio album by the Jimi Hendrix Experience. It was first released by Track Records in the United Kingdom on December 1, 1967, only seven months after the release of the group's highly successful debut album, Are You Experienced. In the United States, Reprise Records delayed the release until the following month. The album reached the top ten in the album charts in both countries.

The album displays several musical styles and critics saw it as demonstrating Jimi Hendrix 's growth as a songwriter. It features " Spanish Castle Magic " and " Little Wing ", two Hendrix compositions that draw on his roots performing with rhythm and blues bands and would remain in his live repertoire throughout his career. Its album cover generated controversy for displaying Hindu religious iconography. It was designed without Hendrix's approval, and he publicly expressed his dissatisfaction.

sections.heading: Where it comes from
sections.text: Stephin Merritt was in a Manhattan gay piano bar, hearing a pianist's takes on Stephen Sondheim songs, when he resolved to move into theatre music. He believed he had a knack for it. He had also read about Charles Ives's 114 Songs that day, and it inspired him. Other influences included Fleetwood Mac, Billie Holiday and Orchestral Manoeuvres in the Dark.

sections.heading: Making it
sections.text: Much of the writing was done in Dick's Bar, a New York bar, and Stephin Merritt said he spent eight hours a day there. He is credited on many instruments, from ukulele and autoharp to musical saw and thunder sheet. Merritt also engineered the record, with help from Jon Berman, Chris Ewen, Claudia Gonson, Eric Masunaga and Charles Newman. Other singers, among them Dudley Klute, LD Beghtol and Shirley Simms, sing on several songs. The songs move between country, synth-pop and free jazz, with sorrowful ballads too. Every song still deals with love, though often with irony or a quirky slant.

sections.heading: What came after

Circus released it in Europe and Australia in May 2000, and Domino reissued it in the UK. Other artists have covered several songs, among them Peter Gabriel with 'The Book of Love' and Superchunk with 'I Don't Want to Get Over You' in 2025.

paragraphs: Raw Power is the third studio album by American rock band the Stooges (credited as Iggy and the Stooges), released on February 7, 1973, by Columbia Records. The album departed from the "groove-ridden, feel-based songs" of the band's first two records in favor of a more anthemic hard rock approach inspired by new guitarist James Williamson, who co-wrote the album's eight songs with singer Iggy Pop.

Pop produced the recording sessions himself with David Bowie assisting in post-production work, though the team were allotted only one day to mix the album and the resulting fidelity was poor. Later reissues have attempted to either correct or enhance the original mix, most notably Pop's 1997 remix, which became notorious for its extreme volume and compression.

B.hook: Pop's first mix put most of the instruments on one side of the stereo and the vocals on the other.

sections.heading: Where it comes from
sections.text: The first two Stooges albums had little commercial success, and the group had split up. Pop's heroin addiction was getting worse when David Bowie stepped in. Pop signed with Columbia as a solo artist and moved to London to make an album with guitarist James Williamson. When they could not find a suitable rhythm section in England, Williamson suggested bringing in Ron and Scott Asheton, both former Stooges. The band reformed under the name Iggy and the Stooges, and the elder Asheton, its founding guitarist, reluctantly agreed to switch to bass.

sections.heading: Making it
sections.text: Staff engineer Mike Ross-Trevor worked on the recording. Pop said Columbia insisted on a ballad for each side of the record: "Gimme Danger" and "I Need Somebody". Because the budget was tight, Bowie reworked seven of the eight songs in one day at Western Sound Recorders in Los Angeles, and Pop kept his own mix of "Search and Destroy". Bowie later recalled that on some songs only three of the 24 tracks were used, and that he often raised and lowered the vocal.

sections.heading: What came after
sections.text: Columbia dropped the band after roughly a year of touring, and the group split up in February 1974. While on day release from rehab, Pop recorded Kill City with Williamson. In 1993 Bomp Records released a selection of the original mixes as Rough Power. In 1996 Columbia invited Pop to remix the whole record for CD, and the remixed edition came out on 22 April 1997. In 2012 both mixes were remastered for a double LP released for Record Store Day, and in 2023 they were remastered again for the album's fiftieth anniversary.

artist: Harold Budd / Brian Eno with Daniel Lanois
title: The Pearl

paragraphs: The Pearl is the second collaborative studio album by Harold Budd and Brian Eno, released in August 1984 by Editions EG and produced by Eno and Daniel Lanois in Hamilton, Ontario. The Pearl is similar to Budd and Eno's previous collaboration, Ambient 2: The Plateaux of Mirror (1980), consisting mostly of subtly treated piano textures, but with more pronounced electronic treatments and nature recordings. The album has been well received by music critics, and is considered by some as a landmark work in ambient music.

B.hook: The trio had no set approach beyond looking for unique moments in the music and capturing them.

sections.heading: Where it comes from
sections.text: The Pearl is the pair's second album together, after Ambient 2: The Plateaux of Mirror (1980). Like Ambient 2, it is built mostly from subtly treated piano textures, with noticeable electronic treatments and recordings of nature added. Budd says the two albums are alike in sound and timbre, and that the likeness was there from the start of production. Ambient 2 came together effortlessly, and the duo believed they could make similar music again without much trouble. Budd said The Pearl was harder to make. He put this down to the duo's naivety on Ambient 2, and to a musical language that had matured since.

sections.heading: Making it
sections.text: For the length of the sessions, the three stayed in one house and worked seven days a week. Recording took two weeks, and finishing the record took 8 to 12 months, as they worked out which pieces suited each other. Eno made most of the aesthetic calls and spent hours working alone, recording pieces at varied speeds. Among the pianos were an acoustic one and electric models by Yamaha and Rhodes. The treatments came from gear that included a Yamaha DX7, a Sequential Circuits Pro One, an AMS digital delay and an Eventide Harmonizer.

listen.text: Budd improvises over humming tones that Eno plays on a Yamaha CS-80, in a single take.

The first plan was a '90s take on The Dark Side of the Moon, covering much the same ground as Virtual Rabbit. Later, he came up with the World Inspection Tour, a role-playing game held overseas for members of his fan club, Hirasawa Bypass. The tour was set for Phuket in Thailand, since the flight was short and the place had little Japanese tourism. On that trial visit he had no clear idea, only a rough picture of the Vietnam War. One night at the Simon Cabaret, where every performer was kathoey, shaped how he saw Thai culture.

sections.heading: Making it
sections.text: Hirasawa did not trust the Thai studio with his gear, so he brought only instrumental 24-track recordings on analog reels to Thailand. There he recorded only vocals over four days, his own and those of Thai performers. Although he was not fluent in Thai, he wrote some lyrics by cross-referencing four language guidebooks. What he first wrote meant something other than he intended, so he rewrote lyrics and melodies on the spot. Masanori Chinzei handled recording and mixing, and Keiko Ueda mastered it. The booklet was shot in Thailand, and it is the only one of his solo albums where he is not the only person pictured.

sections.heading: What came after
sections.text: It was his fifth studio album and his last record with Polydor. He later switched labels to Nippon Columbia.

listen.text: Miss N. of the Phuket Simon Cabaret narrates it, and its lyrics are by her and Hirasawa.
Wisakha Fraytes sings on it, and Miss N. narrates it without a credit.
Miss N. narrates this track as well.

paragraphs: Sim City is the fifth studio album by Japanese musician and composer Susumu Hirasawa, released on August 2, 1995 via Polydor K.K. This is his last record with Polydor, as he would later switch record labels to Nippon Columbia.

A.hook: A lot of it was recorded late at night, once the voices had warmed up or the band had loosened up at its cocktail hour.

facts.label: Recorded
facts.value: July 2006, at Ed Droste's mother's house on Cape Cod

facts.label: Players
facts.value: Christopher Bear (drums, vocals, xylophone, lap steel, glockenspiel), Edward Droste (vocals, keyboard, autoharp, guitar), Daniel Rossen (vocals, guitars, banjo, piano, autoharp), Chris Taylor (clarinet, flute, saxophone, vocals, keyboard, bass, electronics and treatments)

sections.heading: Where it comes from
sections.text: Grizzly Bear was a solo name for vocalist Ed Droste, and Horn of Plenty, released in 2004, was a solo effort. After that, the name grew into a full group, with Horn of Plenty collaborator Christopher Bear, Chris Taylor and Daniel Rossen joining Droste. Christopher Bear said that putting a band together for live shows changed the dynamics and instruments, and helped them find a band sound. Unlike Horn of Plenty, every member of the four-piece had a hand in writing and producing this record.

sections.heading: Making it
sections.text: After about a month of basic tracking, each member added overdubs on their own, and some of them took a long time. Christopher Bear said some of those parts would have been hard with everyone in the room, or with the meter running at a studio. Daniel Rossen's arrival gave the band two main songwriters, and Christopher Bear said the mix of four members' ideas changed the sound most. Droste and Chris Taylor said the lyrics have no real theme, but the album is about the band learning to work together while recording in that house.

sections.heading: What came after
sections.text: Between 2007 and 2011, Adult Swim used several of the album's songs as bumper music, and 'On a Neck, On a Spit' appeared on Reaper, a show on The CW. The first single, 'Knife', came out in May 2007 with an alternate edit of 'Easier' on the other side. Warp20 (Recreated), a 2009 compilation, included Pivot's take on 'Colorado' and Jamie Lidell's take on 'Little Brother'. In 2012, Daniel Rossen recalled that the four of them had been young and eager about making their first record together.

listen.text: Owen Pallett wrote and played the strings on a tune by Droste's great aunt that the band tried to slow down.
G. Lucas Crane contributed tapes to this track.

paragraphs: Yellow House is the second studio album by American rock band Grizzly Bear, released on September 5, 2006, by Warp Records. Produced by bass guitarist and multi-instrumentalist Chris Taylor, the album's title refers to vocalist Ed Droste 's mother's house where the majority of recording took place.

The album is the first to feature both Taylor and vocalist and guitarist Daniel Rossen, and received critical acclaim upon its release, significantly increasing the band's exposure. An EP, Friend, was released the following year featuring material recorded mostly during the same sessions.

A.hook: The label pulled out of an earlier agreement while the album was being recorded, and the print run shrank.

facts.label: Players
facts.value: Grzegorz Ciechowski (vocals, piano, moog), Sławomir Ciesielski (drums), Zbigniew Krzywański (electric guitar, vocals), Paweł Kuczyński (bass guitar)

sections.heading: Making it
sections.text: The album was recorded at Wawrzyszew Sound Studio. Grzegorz Ciechowski wrote the music and lyrics for eight of the nine tracks, and Zbigniew Krzywański shares the music on the ninth track, Obcy astronom. The small run and the poor cover were caused by a change of director at Polton, and with it a change of company policy.

sections.heading: What came after
sections.text: The case went to court, and the band lost it. Reissues followed through the 1990s and 2000s, put out by MMPP, Sound-Pol and Pomaton EMI, and in 2003 the album was part of the Komplet set. In 2002, Nieustanne tango, Psy Pawłowa and Obcy astronom were performed for the last time at a Kombinat concert dedicated to the late Grzegorz Ciechowski.

listen.text: Polton promoted this song abroad in 1985.

paragraphs: Nieustanne tango – drugi studyjny album zespołu Republika, wydany w 1984 przez Polton.
Płyta została nagrana w „Wawrzyszew Sound Studio”. Utwór „Poranna wiadomość” był promowany za granicą w 1985 przez wytwórnię Polton.

Album został wydany w bardzo małym nakładzie, oraz zapakowany w złej jakości okładkę. Było to spowodowane zmianą dyrektora firmy Polton, a co za tym idzie, zmianą polityki firmy. Już w czasie nagrywania firma zrezygnowała z wcześniejszej umowy, czego rezultatem było właśnie zmniejszenie nakładu. Sprawa trafiła do sądu, lecz została przez zespół przegrana. Album został wyprodukowany w nakładzie 46 000 egzemplarzy.
W 2002 roku utwory „Nieustanne tango”, „Psy Pawłowa” i „Obcy astronom” zostały ostatni raz wykonane na koncercie Kombinat poświęconym zmarłemu Grzegorzowi Ciechowskiemu.
